what: Behind the plate sits a wave terrain drawn with bold grid lines (44 cells, line width about 1.6px on screen). A 2×2 plane split into 160 segments heaves up and down by noise height (amplitude .5, frequency 1.6) and drifts slowly with time × .1. The plane lies tilted at 15° (X) and 45° (Y), scaled up 10.6 times, and fades with distance (z 6~32). Once the plane’s top edge touches the top of the screen, and for as long as it takes to travel its own height, the terrain moves toward the camera from z −10 → 7 (power1.out) and fades out. It tilts toward the cursor by .01 of the remaining gap per frame, up to .06 rad. Line color is --kf-line.

options.fade: Share that fades once everything has passed (0 keeps it as is), default 1
options.lean: Max tilt angle toward the cursor (rad), default .06

use: <section class="hero" style="position:relative" data-fx="wave-grid-gl" data-fx-wave-grid-gl="amp: .5; fade: 1"> … Title … </section>
note: A canvas is placed at the very back inside the panel (z-index −1, isolation). It draws only while visible. With reduced motion it is a single terrain that neither flows nor approaches. The original is a glb grid plane + Perlin noise vertex displacement, and this part gives the same shape with our own plane and our own noise (gradient noise) shader

from.where: index.html hero — the original has a wave grid (rotation π/12·π/4, scale 10.648, vertex noise /4×2) moving z −10→7 over scroll 500~5500 and opacity →0 over 500~5000
